title: Composed Workflow Evaluation: LLM + Retrieval + Deterministic Validator + Emulator (Repaired Preregistration)
research_question: Does a reproducible composed evaluation workflow that integrates LLM proposals, retrieval-constrained templating, deterministic validators (Batfish/NetKAT), and an emulator (Mininet) reduce the rate of emulator-detected unsafe/executable faults compared with LLM-only generation on a paired set of natural-language NetOps intents?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary): The composed workflow (LLM → retrieval+templating → deterministic validator → emulator/rollback) yields a lower paired unsafe-execution rate than LLM-only generation (two-sided).
H2 (secondary): The composed workflow yields a lower emulator-fault count per intent (mean counts) than LLM-only generation.
exploratory_questions: E1: How do effects vary by intent complexity strata (simple/moderate/complex)?
E2: What is the observed validator false-negative rate estimated via cross-validator checks (Batfish vs NetKAT) on a held-out coverage set?
E3: What fraction of composed-workflow blocks are false-blocks (valid proposals rejected by validator pipeline)?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic+publicly-derived Intent Corpus (n=200) synthesized from public configuration templates and ticket-style prompts; scope limited to IPv4 routing, ACLs, basic switching, and topology manipulations supported by Mininet/Batfish/NetKAT.
Held-out validator-coverage test set (discovery intents) used only for estimating validator false-negative behavior.
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API provider (hosted_model_api_available = true in capability manifest). Exact model identifier will be fixed in the execution metadata prior to runs and recorded in the disclosure.
All LLM calls are CPU/hosted-API calls only; no local GPU execution.
transformation_scope: Retrieval-constrained templating (local retrieval index of templates), syntax/grammar transformations to vendor-neutral device commands, and exports to Mininet-compatible scripts.
Deterministic validation checks via Batfish (reachability, isolation, ACL compliance) and NetKAT where applicable.
primary_estimand: Per-intent paired difference in unsafe-execution outcome: probability that an intent would produce an emulator-detected unsafe executable fault under LLM-only minus probability under composed workflow (paired on the same intent).
secondary_estimands: Mean emulator-detected fault count per intent per treatment (LLM-only vs composed).
Per-intent false-block rate: proportion of composed-workflow proposals rejected by validator but which the emulator would have accepted (estimated via targeted replays).
Per-intent latency and token-usage cost per treatment (for cost-effectiveness reporting).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory corpus: n=200 intents sampled deterministically from the synthetic/public template pool stratified into three complexity strata (simple: 80, moderate: 80, complex: 40). For each intent, run two paired treatments: (A) LLM-only generation and (B) Composed workflow. All intents are processed on the same deterministic environment seeds. Discovery (validator-coverage) set: 50 additional intents (stratified) used only for estimating validator false-negative rates and cross-validator checks.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired-test on binary unsafe-execution outcomes per intent using McNemar's test (two-sided). Report 95% Wilson CIs for proportions, absolute and relative risk reductions, and number-needed-to-protect. Secondary analysis: compare mean emulator-fault counts using paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (or paired t-test if normality holds per diagnostics) with bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 bootstrap replicates). Report exact p-values and effect sizes. All primary analyses use preregistered seeds and deterministic scoring scripts; exploratory subgroup analyses are explicitly labeled exploratory and multiplicity-controlled as below.
multiplicity_plan: Primary hypothesis H1 is single confirmatory test. Secondary and exploratory tests (intent-strata, false-block rate, emulator-fault counts) are exploratory; when reporting multiple exploratory p-values, apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control at q=0.10 and report unadjusted p-values alongside adjusted thresholds.
missingness_plan: Technical failures (API/network/infrastructure) are handled deterministically: automatic retry policy of up to 2 additional attempts spaced by exponential backoff (total attempts=3). If LLM call still fails, mark the run as technical-failure and exclude the affected paired intent from the primary per-protocol analysis; simultaneously report an intention-to-run (ITT) sensitivity analysis where failed calls are imputed as 'unsafe' for LLM-only or 'unsafe' for composed workflow depending on conservative worst-case assumptions; all exclusions, retry counts, and raw logs are recorded and disclosed.

risk_factors: Retrieval index contamination (inadvertent inclusion of harmful or environment-specific commands).
Validator-emulator mismatch (Batfish/NetKAT checks not covering all semantic intent modes).
API outages or rate-limiting leading to missing paired measurements.
detection_procedures: Deterministic checksum+versioning for retrieval index snapshots; any change flags contamination and invalidates affected runs.
Automated cross-validator consistency checks: for validator-coverage set, run Batfish and NetKAT deterministically and record disagreements; high disagreement rate triggers sensitivity reporting.
Automated runtime logging of API error codes and deterministic flagging of rate-limit or outage events.
item_flagging_rules: Flag any intent or template whose retrieval snapshot checksum differs from preregistered snapshot and exclude from confirmatory analysis; flagged items reported in contamination audit.
Flag any composed workflow output that contains tokens matching a pre-registered harmful-command regex; such outputs are rejected automatically and recorded (no execution).
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis excludes contaminated/flagged items (per deterministic rules) and reports a contamination audit table. Sensitivity analyses re-run including flagged items with explicit labels and, where feasible, with conservative imputations; all deviations are logged.
residual_uncertainty: Residual risk that retrieval corpus omissions or unseen template variants alter effect estimates.
Residual miscoverage by validators for properties not expressible in the chosen checks (semantic intent-level misses).

budget_scenarios.description: Minimal-budget execution: no LLM regeneration retries in composed workflow; no validator-coverage discovery set.
models: hosted LLM API (model identifier to be fixed at preregistration)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-intent model calls: LLM-only = 1 call; composed workflow (no retries) = 1 call. Combined per-intent = 2 calls. 200 intents × 2 = 400 total calls. This fits capability_manifest maximum_planned_model_calls (10000) and the manifest wall-clock allowance; however it omits validator-coverage tests and uses no retries (conservative cost).

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended tradeoff: bounded regeneration attempts for composed workflow and a modest validator-coverage discovery set to estimate validator false-negative behavior.
models: hosted LLM API (model identifier to be fixed at preregistration)
transformations: deterministic validators: Batfish and NetKAT (used for coverage set and cross-checks)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Derivation: For each confirmatory intent: LLM-only = 1 call; composed workflow = up to 3 calls (initial + up to 2 deterministic regeneration attempts) → 4 calls/intent → 200 intents × 4 = 800 calls. Discovery set (50 intents) run with same per-intent budget: 50 × 4 = 200 calls. Total = 800 + 200 = 1,000 planned model calls. This is within the manifest limit of 10,000 and allows bounded retry coverage plus validator-coverage tests to quantify validator false-negative rates. All counts are deterministic and logged.

budget_scenarios.description: Exhaustive execution: more regeneration attempts and larger validator-coverage set for stress testing and sensitivity analyses.
models: hosted LLM API (model identifier to be fixed at preregistration)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Derivation: For each confirmatory intent: LLM-only = 1 call; composed workflow = up to 5 calls (initial + up to 4 regeneration attempts) → 6 calls/intent → 200 × 6 = 1,200 calls. Discovery set (100 intents) at same per-intent budget: 100 × 6 = 600 calls. Total = 1,200 + 600 = 1,800 planned model calls. Still within manifest limit (10,000). This scenario supports stronger validator coverage estimation and stress-testing regeneration; higher CPU/latency and token costs are expected and will be reported.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired per-intent absolute difference in unsafe-execution probability (LLM-only minus composed workflow)
power_plan.target_effect: Detect an absolute reduction in unsafe-execution rate of ~7.5 percentage points (e.g., from 15% baseline unsafe rate to 7.5%).
power_plan.clustering_unit: Intent (paired within-intent comparison between two treatments).
power_plan.calculation_method: Paired (within-intent) McNemar test (exact/approximate) for binary outcomes. Approximate sample-size sensitivity computed using standard normal approximation to McNemar discordant counts and bootstrap verification on observed discordant patterns.
assumptions: Alpha = 0.05 (two-sided), desired power ≈ 0.80 for primary confirmatory test.

Baseline unsafe-execution rate under LLM-only ≈ 0.10–0.20 (plausible range based on supplied prototype evidence summaries); detectable absolute reduction target ≈ 6–8 percentage points with n=200 pairs depending on discordant proportions.
Paired design reduces between-intent variance compared to unpaired designs; discordant-pair proportion assumed ≥0.10 for power approximations.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With n=200 paired intents and alpha=0.05, a two-sided McNemar-test is approximately powered to detect absolute paired reductions in the ~6–8% range when baseline unsafe rates are 10–20% and discordant-pair proportions are moderate (≈0.10–0.20). Exact MDE depends on observed discordant counts; bootstrap sensitivity analyses are preregistered.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute MDE under baseline unsafe rates of 5%, 10%, 15%, and 25%.
Bootstrap 95% CIs for risk reductions (10,000 replicates).
Per-strata (simple/moderate/complex) power diagnostics; treat these as exploratory if underpowered.

transformation_families: Vendor-agnostic normalization and regex-based syntax checks
semantic_equivalence_checks: Automated unit tests comparing intended post-configuration network properties (reachability matrix) with properties implied by generated config using Batfish; deterministic pass/fail.
Round-trip parser checks: exported Mininet script -> read-back parser -> canonical form equals canonical form of initial template (checksum-based).
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject generated outputs automatically if syntax validators fail, if grammar regex mismatches vendor-allowed token sets, or if outputs contain tokens matching harmful-command regex; rejected outputs trigger deterministic regeneration attempts up to the preregistered retry limit.
If after max retries output still rejected, mark as 'validator-block' and record as composed-workflow block (potential false-block).
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated audit of 10% random sample of confirmatory intents using cross-validator consistency checks (Batfish vs NetKAT where applicable) and deeper emulator replay to detect validator misses; sampling deterministic (seeded RNG) and reproducible.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Publishable deterministic unit test suite that verifies mapping from template variables to emitted device commands across a small set of representative vendor-normalized templates; tests run automatically pre-execution and post-generation to assert syntactic conformance.
residual_risks: Validators (Batfish/NetKAT) do not cover all semantic intent interpretations (residual semantic intent-mismatch risk).
Regex/syntax checks may not capture subtle vendor-specific runtime behaviors not reproducible in Mininet.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: External-validity: how Mininet/Batfish/NetKAT emulator and validators map to real vendor devices and large production topologies (acknowledged and bounded to emulator scope).
Representativeness of the synthetic/public intent corpus relative to enterprise heterogeneity (vendors, protocols, and ticket styles).
Deterministic validators' blindspots for properties not expressible in the chosen formal checks (semantic intent interpretation outside reachability/ACL checks).
Potential model/API rate-limiting or provider-specific nondeterminism; deterministic logging and contingency are in place but residual timing-related effects may remain.
